_meta.note: Drawn at the end of any turn you overclocked 1+ times (clean runs draw none; a shutdown draws an extra). The 'copies' field gives how many physical copies to make so the assembled deck matches the sim's consWeights {int1:20,int2:8,cashLoss:15,cashGain:12,repLoss:10,repGain:10,modLoss:5,nothing:20}. Total copies below = 24. repLoss is an HONEST setback (peer review) and hits the Reputation pile directly, never disrepute. Real-history flavour lives here.

cards.name: A Frayed Thread
cards.fiction: A small thing comes loose in the past — a letter delivered a day late, a face remembered that shouldn't be. Nothing the present notices yet. But the timeline notices.

cards.name: Double-Booked
cards.fiction: For ninety seconds, two versions of the same street corner in 1908 exist at once. They resolve. Mostly.

cards.name: The Wrong Pocket
cards.fiction: Something modern was left behind down there — a coin, a button, a fibre. Some future archaeologist is going to have a very confusing afternoon.

cards.name: Cascade
cards.fiction: One change tugs another, which tugs three more. By the time anyone traces it back, the knot has pulled tight across two centuries.

cards.name: Paradox Feedback
cards.fiction: The machine hums at a frequency you've never heard before and the lights in the lab — every lab, on the timeline — flicker in unison. That can't be good.

cards.name: Customs Trouble
cards.fiction: Bringing back period currency seemed clever until you tried to spend it. The numismatist who 'authenticated' it took a generous cut and asked no questions.
cards.effect: Lose 2 Cash (down to a minimum of 0).

cards.name: Grant Clawback
cards.fiction: The funding committee has 'concerns about methodology.' They always do, right after a noisy jump.
cards.effect: Lose 3 Cash (down to a minimum of 0).

cards.name: Equipment Loss
cards.fiction: Something didn't come back through the door in one piece. Replacing it is neither cheap nor covered by the warranty.
cards.effect: Lose 2 Cash (down to a minimum of 0).

cards.name: A Private Buyer
cards.fiction: A discreet collector hears what you've been up to and makes an unsolicited offer for 'anything you don't strictly need.' You sell them a crate of off-cuts.

cards.name: Patent Windfall
cards.fiction: A material you glanced at in the field turns out to be trivially patentable in the present. The licence cheque clears before you've finished the paperwork.

cards.name: Peer Review
cards.fiction: A rival re-examines your last paper and finds a genuine error — the dating was off, the provenance shaky. They are not wrong. This is the system working as intended; it still stings.

cards.name: Retraction
cards.fiction: One of your findings can't be reproduced, and you do the decent thing and withdraw it. Better caught now than built upon. The pile gets a little shorter.

cards.name: Corroboration
cards.fiction: A find someone else made in the present quietly confirms something you published months ago. Vindication is the slowest and sweetest currency in science.

cards.name: An Invited Lecture
cards.fiction: Word of your last expedition reaches the right ears, and the invitation is to the kind of hall that doesn't usually let your sort in. You give a good talk.

cards.name: Module Strain
cards.fiction: You pushed one system past where it wanted to go, and a level of it gives out — a coil, a lens, a seal. It can be rebuilt, but not tonight.
cards.effect: Lose one level from a machine module of your choice (minimum level 1; Stabiliser minimum 2). If nothing can drop, ignore.

cards.name: A Quiet Return
cards.fiction: You half-expect the lights to flicker or the phone to ring with bad news. Neither happens. The door closes behind you and the timeline holds. You exhale.
cards.effect: No effect. This one was clean.

cards.name: Near Miss
cards.fiction: Something almost went wrong — you felt the machine catch, saw the needle twitch — and then it didn't. You'll tell this one at parties as if you were never worried.

cards.name: Lab Superstition
cards.fiction: The team insists the jump was cursed and performs the usual rituals — the tea, the tapping, the one rude word said to the Capacitor. It works, in that nothing happens.
